name: Frank Smith
role: Bad Lands hunter; brother of Vic Smith
bio: Frank Smith and his brother gave the Cow Boy's Bad Lands museum petrified wood, gypsum and other specimens in early 1884. He and his brother Vic Smith moved to Medora from Bismarck in May 1885, and that summer he managed the floor at a dance and joined the Marquise de Mores' hunting party to the Big Horn country.

moments.label: Gave gypsum specimens to the paper's museum

mentions: Frank Smith, not to be outdone by his brother, yesterday brought in a petrifaction of a piece of cottonwood which seems to have petrified after the wood had dried and the veins sepa…
The best specimens of gypsum we have yet seen were brought in and added to our collection by Frank Smith. The Smith Brothers alone, if they keep on, will give us a splendid collection by fall.
Johnny Goodall, Frank Smith and Rev. Silas Cheval are the latest contributors to our Bad Lands museum. The latter "held up" a passing freight and secured a good specimen of galena.
Again has Frank Smith come to the front with valuable additions to our Bad Lands curiosities. If we don't have a collection to be proud of it won't be the fault of the Smith brothers.
Again has Frank Smith placed our Bad Lands museum under obligations to him. One specimen has the plain print of water flags upon it, although it was found on the top of a high butte.
Vic Smith and his brother Frank came in Saturday night from Bismarck. They will make Medora their home.
…and very much of the pleasure of the evening was due to the efficient services of the floor manager Mr. Frank Smith.
